messages:
irma: Quick sync  we need a clear runtime contract for routing policy artifacts. I want a single lightweight object the runtime can consume: "route_ledger". Questions: mutation budget, explainability, and debug overrides.

sam: Route_ledger sounds good. Main constraint: p99 decision time must be <200us for the fast path. That basically forces a pre-compiled structure.

anya: Pre-compiled makes sense but we should keep an interpreter fallback for debug and experiments. Suggest the ledger contain an optional `fallback_snippet` plus a `compat_stamp`.

ops: We also need safe mutation limits. Propose `nudging_budget_ms` and `nudging_budget_ops`. Runtime can apply deviant deltas to route scores but only while budget remains. Budget resets per-request.

irma: Example ledger sketch:

```
{
  "ledger_version": "1",
  "policy_key": "tiered-geo-v1",
  "routes": [
    {"rid":"eu-1","base_score":900,"region":"eu-west","explain":"low_latency_eu"},
    {"rid":"us-2","base_score":700,"region":"us-central","explain":"cost_balance"}
  ],
  "fallback_snippet": "if region == 'emergency' then -10000 end",
  "max_runtime_delta_pct": 15,
  "nudging_budget_ms": 2,
  "compat_stamp": "2026-03-21-abc123"
}
```

anya: Nice. Two additions: `delta_ttl_ms` (so runtime deltas expire) and `per_tenant_delta_override` field so enterprise tenants can allow larger deltas.

sam: Good point. Also require `explain_id` per clause to make stack traces deterministic. No opaque blobs.

ops: On testing: we need a `shadow-reconcile` job that replays traffic and compares route assignments when ledger is used vs interpreter. If mismatch beyond threshold, flag. This can be integrated into CI and into canary gating.

infra-bot: deployment note: policy-compiler:v3 scheduled to staging at 70% canary.

irma: Runtime behaviour rules proposal: 1) runtime loads ledger; 2) compute base scores; 3) apply probe & capacity deltas bounded by `max_runtime_delta_pct` and `nudging_budget`; 4) if ledger fallback_snippet present and compiled flow fails, run snippet with execution cap; 5) always emit explain tags.

anya: About emit: standard tags should be `policy.ledger_version`, `policy.eval_mode`, `policy.delta_applied`, `policy.delta_source`, `policy.matched_explain_id`. For fallback runs add `policy.fallback_exec_time_ms`.

sam: Also track `policy.delta_origin_hash` so we can trace which signal produced the delta. Useful in postmortems.

ops: Rollout plan: shadow -> 5% canary -> run `shadow-reconcile` on canary traffic -> auto-checks (route distribution parity, latency tail, error rates) -> advance. We should also allow on-demand tenant toggle to force interpreter for a single tenant for debugging with header `X-Policy-Mode: interpreter` but gated by ACL.

irma: Performance guard: if fallback_snippet execution exceeds `nudging_budget_ms`, abort and emit `policy.fallback_timeout=true`. Runtime must not block request.

anya: Security note: fallback_snippet must be sanitized server-side; no network calls; bounded ops. We should maintain a whitelist of functions available to snippet.

sam: I'm worried about complexity of `per_tenant_delta_override`. Maybe start without it, but add tenant-scoped feature flag so we can allow specific tenants larger deltas during experiments.

ops: Agree incremental approach. Add field `tenant_flags_allowed: ["big_delta"]` to ledger so compiler can opt-in tenants. Runtime still must check central flag store.

infra-bot: job: policy-sim-v1 kicked off.

irma: Ok next actions: I'll author RFC with ledger JSON schema, runtime flow pseudocode, telemetry spec, budget semantics, and canary playbook. Who wants to review?

anya: I'll review telemetry and security constraints.

sam: I'll review performance and explain hooks.

ops: I'll own canary gating and `shadow-reconcile` CI job.

irma: Thanks all. Planning to file RFC by Monday EOD. :white_check_mark:
